items.summary:
▲ Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, an upgrade that beats Opus 5.5 on most of its own benchmarks at a lower price.

The key idea is 1 model with 2 safeguard levels. Fable 5.2 runs classifiers that block high-risk cyber and research-biology requests, then hands those to Opus 4.8 or Opus 5. Mythos 5.2 is the same model without those blocks, for vetted orgs only.

On FrontierCode 2.0, Fable 5.2 scores 49.1% at Xhigh effort, vs 45.5% for Opus 5.5 and 42.8% for GPT-6 Astra. At High effort it matches Opus 5.5's best score for roughly half the cost per task. It is a trade-off though: Gemini 4 Carbon still leads AutomationBench (53.9% vs 51.4%), and every score is self-reported.

Pricing is $8 / $40 per million tokens, with a 1M-token context window and 128K output. Fast mode runs up to 2.5x faster at $16 / $80. API ID: claude-fable-5-2......

items.title: Meta’s AI age-check goes global: Can it protect teens? | Mental Health News | Al Jazeera
items.summary:
Meta has rolled out artificial intelligence (AI)-powered age-estimation technology worldwide in an effort to better detect teenage users who signed up for its social media platforms with an adult’s birth date.

The world’s largest social media company announced the change on Monday, saying that millions more young people worldwide would be placed in its Teen Accounts following the implementation of the new technology amid concerns that its platforms have failed to protect teenagers. [...] The AI searches a user’s account to find “contextual clues” that point to their age. Examples given by Meta include “birthday celebrations or mentions of school grades”.

It also uses “visual cues” in pictures and videos on the account, but Meta says that this does not extend to facial recognition. [...] Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Threads, said on Monday that it had started using its AI age-estimation system on Instagram accounts around the world.

“Since first introducing this technology, we’ve been placing more teens in age-appropriate protections and are encouraged by the results. Based on that success, today we’re expanding this technology globally,” the company said.

items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là một hàm mà khi lấy đạo hàm sẽ cho ra \( x^2 \). Để tìm nguyên hàm, ta sử dụng công thức:

\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C
\]

Trong trường hợp này, \( n = 2 \):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là \( \frac{x^3}{3} + C \), trong đó \( C \) là hằng số tùy ý.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
